title: Your family

lines: WHAT DID HE DO AT HOME?
cards: A man named al-Aswad put a plain question to Aisha: what did the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, do at home? Not in the mosque, not leading anyone. At home.
Her answer, in Sahih al-Bukhari: he would be busy serving his family, and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to pray. That's the whole report. No miracle in it.
A man helping around the house, then stopping for prayer. A strangely ordinary thing to have been remembered.

teach.b: That report sets the order of things. Service at home and prayer aren't rivals; the same person does both, in the same afternoon. Then the house itself.
In another hadith in Bukhari, the Prophet tells his followers to pray some of their prayers in their houses, and not to make their houses like graves.

teach.h: DON'T MAKE YOUR HOUSE A GRAVE.
teach.b: The picture is stark: a house with no prayer in it is likened to a grave. Praying together: one can lead and the others stand behind in a row.
A parent leads, a child stands beside or behind, and the prayer is said at the same pace. Small children wander in and out of it.
In Bukhari there's a report of the Prophet praying while carrying his little granddaughter Umamah, setting her down when he went down in prostration and picking her up when he stood.
The tradition didn't wait for a quiet house to pray in one.
And families as they really are. Some homes are all Muslim. Some have a new Muslim and parents who aren't.
Some have a spouse from another faith or none. Praying together can mean one person praying while another sits nearby in quiet, or a family sharing a meal and saying bismillah before it.
In surah Ta Ha, Allah tells the Prophet to bid his household to prayer and to be patient in it. Patient is the word to keep. Habits at home grow slowly, and nobody is helped by being pushed.

how: Muslim families may pray some prayers together at home, with one person leading and the others standing behind in a row and children joining as they learn, following the hadith that encourages praying some prayers in the house.

o: the first place practice is lived: serving at home, praying there
the relatives who must all be Muslim before you can pray
a household where only the father is meant to pray

p: he served his family, then went to pray
bid your household to prayer, be patient

s: the Prophet left all housework to others
Aisha said he would be busy serving his family until the time for prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari).
a hadith tells of the Prophet praying while carrying his granddaughter
he carried Umamah, setting her down when he went down in prostration and picking her up when he stood (Sahih al-Bukhari).
prayer is only meant for the mosque
the Prophet told his followers to pray some prayers in their houses and not make them like graves.

games.q: you're about to pray, and your small granddaughter won't let go of you. what did the Prophet do?
o: prayed while carrying her, setting her down to prostrate.
sent her out of the room.
games.why: Sahih al-Bukhari tells of him praying while carrying Umamah, setting her down when he went down in prostration and picking her up when he stood.

practice: Bring to mind the people you live with, or the family you're closest to, one face at a time, and let one small act of service come to mind for one of them: a dish washed, a bag carried, a phone call returned.
If you pray, choose one prayer today and invite someone at home to stand with you for it, simply, without a speech; if you or your family don't pray, one quiet moment shared at a meal is enough.

wordCard.voice: Your family. The first place practice is lived: serving at home, and praying there too. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: family, household, a person's people.

carryVoice: Your line: pray together. Service first, then the prayer, in the same afternoon. See you tomorrow.
